name: Spin Scooters: Unlocking the Problem
description: Investigate why Spin's electric scooter usage on UCSD campus has declined over recent quarters. Analyze the root cause, evaluate a proposed tap-to-ride solution using student IDs, calculate financial viability, and deliver a final recommendation to the CEO.

content.prompt: Our client is Spin, a company that operates electric scooters on the UC San Diego campus. Historically, usage was strong, especially during peak hours when students needed quick rides in between classes. However, average monthly rides have declined steadily over the past few quarters, resulting in lower revenue and overall profitability. Spin has hired you at TCG to investigate this decline and explore potential solutions to reverse the trend. List any clarifying questions you would ask the client and brainstorm potential reasons for the revenue decline, including examples of how each might appear in Spin’s operations.

rows: Are scooters not being maintained or broken?
Is it the app that's causing issues?
Are there multiple refunds that need to be processed? Are they costly?
Are there fewer students going to classes post-COVID?
Spotty connectivity in busy areas could cause issues
Do people prefer buses, shuttles, or walking?
Persistent failed attempts may cause users to become frustrated, influence their friends against Spin
Continually unsatisfied users cause brand perception to go down, and value decreases
Technical fixes like Bluetooth unlock, QR code/offline unlock, and UCSD Wi-Fi partnership
Operational fixes like placing scooters in better-connected areas speed up refunds
Pricing/incentives like ride credits or discounts to rebuild trust

content.prompt: Using survey data, you have found that a primary reason for the usage drop is that students are often unable to unlock scooters due to spotty cellular service on parts of campus. To combat this, Spin's team has developed a solution that achieves a 100% success rate: a tap-to-ride system that allows students to unlock scooters using their UCSD ID, with no cellular connection required. Develop a framework to assess whether this tap-to-ride feature is a worthwhile investment for Spin.

rows: No need for a cellular signal, and increases reliability
Builds trust, better brand reception, and reputation - fewer complaints
Faster unlock and smoother rides, reducing time to get to class
Fewer refunds, standardizing Spin access across campus
Student ID carried regularly, existing methods of payment (Triton cash, dining dollars)
Expected increase monthly - ROI soon, long-term savings
Strengthens partnership with UCSD- can be implemented in other big campuses with similar problems
Shift from app to ID costs time and money
Dependence on UCSD IT system for regulation→ delays
Installation cost and effort, high upfront investment cost
Marketing cost of the new feature
Reduced app engagement, hard to gain user data, market, etc.

content.prompt: As part of your evaluation, Spin has provided you with the following operational and financial data related to their estimated implementation and projected impact. Spin expects a 30% increase in monthly rides with this feature. The following exhibit includes these cost estimates. Using the exhibit, determine whether Spin will break even within 12 months.

images.alt: Spin Scooter Financial and Cost Data

content.prompt: The CEO of Spin is at UCSD right now, asking what your findings have been and whether this proposal would be a good idea. Finalize your recommendation and present your conclusion and next steps to her.

rows: Spin should implement the UCSD ID tap-to-ride feature across its scooter fleet. The investment addresses the core usability issue that caused ridership decline and is expected to become profitable within the first year.

Identified the reason for declining usage (spotty cellular connectivity), created a pros/cons framework for the proposed solution, calculated estimated profit of $96,200 in the first year, demonstrating positive ROI.
Not all students may immediately switch to using their UCSD ID cards, especially those accustomed to the app or upperclassmen who might not carry their ID cards with them.
Integration with UCSD's ID system may face delays or technical complications.
Bluetooth hardware may require more frequent upkeep or troubleshooting than expected.
Reduced app engagement could limit future data insights and monetization opportunities.
Develop a marketing plan focused on ERC and other dead-zone areas. Consider offering small ride credits to early adopters for the first month to drive usage.
Find a way to track ridership growth, ID unlock usage rate, and refund reduction.
Collaborate with UCSD IT + Student Affairs to plan integration timing and student communication.
